flavor_spans.text: It's quiet. Your footsteps are soft on the carpet. How can a staircase be so long?

Hot summer winds blew
the day you walked in.
But in here,
stale air.

You stand upon the landing.
Each wing more difficult than the last.
Structures are built one tile at a time.

The tiles weren't enough.
The yen wasn't enough either.
One more wing,
that will be enough.
In the storeroom, tea sets sit in lacquer boxes with the cups already poured. Ah, but The House has little patience for ceremony.

One lantern
shows the next step.
The rest of the wing
is
dark.
Someone scratched a tally into the bannister — seven marks, then eight, then the numbers stop and start again lower down, as if the wall moved overnight.

The door you come through
is not the door
you leave by.
Eventually you stop checking.

Dust falls down
through the soft lantern light.
Onto an old carpet.

Another table, another hand to be played.
You walk faster.
When you fell last time, The House took your yen and your relics. You started again with someone else's leftovers in your pockets and pretended that was a fresh start.
The House rewards a fat purse with interest, the way a host refills your cup so you'll stay at the table. You know who wins in aggregate. You stay anyway.
The House will remember you when you're gone. It cares for its guests, in its own way.
"We have a winner! You, our most honored contestant and guest!" A banner said that. The banner has been here longer than you have.
Tiles clack somewhere behind the wall — Melds being played in a room with no door. You pause on the landing. The sound stops when you listen for it.
The gambling house shut its doors to the world years ago. Inside, the lamps still burn. You wonder who keeps the ledger.

Your footsteps
echo behind you.
But when you stop:
Silence.

Thirty-seven steps
today.
Yesterday
there were forty-one.
A hope-shattered gambler sat on this step once. The cushion still holds their shape. You sit beside it and don't ask how long they've been gone.
If your tea starts swirling in the cup, drink up before it swallows you.
A faded placard: "Please enjoy our complimentary buffet of lost souls in the next wing!"
The House tea will never quench your thirst. You keep drinking it anyway.
The four gentlemen laugh amongst themselves. What would flowers find so funny?
Rumor has it every relic is the soul of a player who delved too deep.
Four great blessings: Skill, luck, a few tiles up your sleeve, and a little gold to bend the rules.
They say the tiles are made from the bones of players of old.
Was that cackling? or the distant clack of tiles?
"Congratulations, Esteemed Winner! See your hostess for a complimentary beverage" reads a tattered banner. No hostess but the creaking stairs.
A crude map is carved in the bannister. The rooms you entered are not on it.
The railing is carved with a repeating map-like pattern of rooms and hallways.
Money, tiles, time. Everything flows downstream.
Every prize has its price.
You can't afford to lose.
No windows. No clocks. No way but down.
Intrusive image: You are watching yourself float downstream, discarded.
The walls are closing in. Draw a tile before it's too late.
Survival is like plucking the moon from the bottom of the stairwell.
Ten thousand ways to lose. How many to survive?
A color flush is monochrome in this light.
Do chickens even have hands?
